correctness.rationale: For every n>=1 and fixed 0<a<b<c, Legendre parity and the explicit positive-coefficient expansion establish the finite-degree reflected threshold. Fixed exterior Laplace asymptotics give |pi_n(c)| and its coefficient. Orthogonality, Markov bound on (P_n^2)', midpoint discrepancy, and independence of Gaussian squares yield S_n/[M_n/(2n+1)] -> 1 in probability when d_n/n^4 -> infinity. Slutsky and continuity give the chi-square critical window, its sharp constant q/[pi sqrt(z^2-1)], and the three domination regimes. A standalone standard-library script passes 204 finite checks; experiments are not used as an infinite proof. No claims for other polynomials or optimal dimension condition.

value.rationale: Single rare eigenvalue outliers are a concrete failure mode for spectral-density-calibrated accelerated iterations. The theorem distinguishes two structurally different boundaries: the absolute reflected-outlier contraction boundary c=a+b and the random relative-error takeover crossover d_n~q^(2n). The exact chi-square critical law quantifies risk of outlier domination even on the contracting side and provides a parameter-dependent high-dimensional benchmark. This is more than a routine finite polynomial identity, and the scope and sufficient dimension assumption are explicit.
